title: Malaria — WHO baseline (draft)
summary: WHO malaria baseline for primary care: parasitological confirmation, ACT for uncomplicated disease, parenteral artesunate for severe disease, and prevention. National malaria programmes set the first-line ACT and pregnancy guidance via overlays. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.
diagnosis: Confirm malaria parasitologically (RDT or microscopy) before treatment — do NOT treat on clinical suspicion alone where testing is available.
Identify species and assess for severity features.
treatmentUncomplicated: Uncomplicated P. falciparum: a WHO-recommended artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT), e.g. artemether-lumefantrine, for 3 days, weight-banded.
P. vivax / ovale: ACT or chloroquine (per local resistance) PLUS primaquine for radical cure after G6PD assessment.
Counsel to return if symptoms persist or danger signs appear.
treatmentSevere: Severe malaria: parenteral artesunate (IV/IM) for at least 24h and until able to tolerate oral, then complete a full ACT course.
Pre-referral rectal artesunate for young children when injectable treatment and referral are delayed.
Manage complications: hypoglycaemia, severe anaemia, seizures, acidosis.
pregnancy: Treat per trimester following national guidance; severe malaria in pregnancy is an emergency.
Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) with SP in moderate-to-high transmission areas.
prevention: Insecticide-treated nets (ITNs); indoor residual spraying where indicated.
Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) and perennial chemoprevention in eligible settings; RTS,S/R21 vaccine per programme.
redFlags: Impaired consciousness, convulsions, respiratory distress, shock, jaundice, severe anaemia, inability to tolerate orals — treat as severe malaria and refer.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should set the national first-line ACT, endemicity/transmission setting, and pregnancy regimens.
